prompts.prompt: Please tell us what you are interested in studying at college and why.

intl_finance.document: Affidavit of Financial Support (AOFS) plus certified bank statements in English showing funds for the first year's tuition and living expenses and a comparable amount for each later year, with statements of the amounts and sources of funds. Applicants who say they will not apply for need-based aid must also submit the International Financial Information form in the WashU Pathway.

deadlines.label: International Financial Information form (applicants not applying for need-based aid)
deadlines.note: Required for the application to be complete; no separate date is published, so it follows the application deadline for your decision plan.

deadlines.label: I-20 financial statements (enrolling students)
deadlines.note: WashU requires these before a Form I-20 can be processed; no fixed date is published.

intl_finance.notes: The page says to get two original copies (with original signatures) of both the sponsor's letter and the bank letter, and keep a copy for the visa, because some embassies verify them. Financial aid offers may be deducted from the amount to be certified. International students are eligible for need-based aid only if they apply during the admission process (CSS Profile due with the aid deadline for each plan); that is a financial aid step, not the I-20 proof of funds.

notes: WashU no longer has an optional writing supplement for fall 2027; the only college-specific written item is the 250-word response above (the same question is listed on the first-year international page). The page does not say whether the limit is a maximum or exact, only '250-word response'. Separate from the application: priority scholarship applications (Signature Scholar Programs: Danforth, Ervin, Rodriguez) include a 250-word short answer in the WashU Pathway after the application is submitted (priority date December 16, 2026), and the Nemerov Writing Scholars Program takes a writing portfolio; the scholarship question text is not published on the pages read, so it is not listed. An optional video supplement also exists. Application deadlines: Early Action and Early Decision I November 2, Early Decision II and Regular Decision January 4.
